To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Liver transplantation (LT) is an effective therapy for hepatoblastoma (HB), and for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC); and (2) the risk of tumour recurrence is high in HB patients who have received chemotherapy, but not in those who received surgery only, or in those who received chemotherapy after surgery.

the overall survival rate after liver transplantation for malignant tumour in children is high, and that the survival rate is higher for patients who receive liver transplantation before the age of 2 years and those who receive liver transplantation for hepatoblastoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel methods for the synthesis and characterisation of novel compounds and the study of their chemical, biological and physical properties.
the development of a novel, noninvasive method for the diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma in children.
the development of new methods for the treatment of malignant tumors in children, in particular for liver transplantation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
liver transplantation is an appropriate and effective treatment for unresectable primary liver malignancies, and that it can be considered for unresectable secondary liver malignancies.
the use of liver transplantation for the treatment of malignant hepatic tumours in children is not justified.
the risk of malignancies is not significantly increased after liver transplantation in children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
liver transplant recipients with malignancy had been in a position to live for an additional 5 years.
the most significant factor for survival after liver transplantation for hepatoblastoma is tumour stage.
the liver is a very important organ that is responsible for a number of important metabolic functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to be more aware of the risks and side effects of the drugs we are prescribing to children and adolescents.
we can use the liver as a model to better understand the mechanisms of aging and to test interventions to extend healthspan.
we need to be cautious about the use of the term'malignant' when discussing paediatric liver tumours.
